topics.label: Introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture themes, connects back to recent practicals, and outlines the day's learning objectives.

topics.label: Tumor virology and assays for cellular transformation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how the study of transforming tumor viruses revealed cellular proto-oncogenes and led to laboratory assays for measuring malignant transformation.

topics.label: Classification and genetic mechanisms of oncogenes and tumor suppressors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define the major categories of cancer-associated mutations and illustrate dominant and recessive mutational mechanisms using the Rb and p53 pathways.

topics.label: Mechanisms and cellular consequences of genetic instability
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the distinctions between sequence and chromosome instability, the specific DNA repair and mitotic failures that cause them, and their downstream cellular stresses.

topics.label: Multi-step tumorigenesis and hereditary cancer predispositions
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how cumulative genetic alterations and inherited predispositions drive cancer progression across sporadic and familial syndromes.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and recommended reading
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture, offers recommended reading, and previews the next lecture on the hallmarks of cancer.
